gaps.construct: multi-clause function heads matching literal strings ("Z", "z") and list destructuring [Sign, H1, H2 | MinutesDiff] = Tz
gaps.description: The doc's only matching form is `choose` over variants and maybe values; there is no list, cons or string pattern, so the clause heads become if tests and the destructure becomes explicit length checks and indexing.

gaps.construct: taking characters and substrings of a string ($:, [H1, H2])
gaps.description: No character type, character literal or substring operation exists; `character i of tz` and `characters i until j of tz` are invented.

gaps.construct: let-it-crash: badmatch, case_clause and badarg exceptions on malformed input
gaps.description: Scribe requires every failure to be named in `fails with`; the three implicit crash kinds collapse into one invented BadOffset, which changes the failure surface the original exposes.

gaps.construct: converting the callee's failure into a different failure name
gaps.description: `handle` wraps a whole block; renaming NotANumber to BadOffset for one expression needed a separate helper operation.
The doc does not say whether unused parameters are allowed or need marking.
Unary minus is not shown; written as 0 - adjustment.

invented_syntax: characters i until j of tz
choice used as a set of failure names (OffsetError)
notes: Erlang's crash-on-mismatch style has no counterpart: Scribe forces malformed-input handling to be written out, which made the translation longer but arguably more honest. The doc never shows how failure names are declared (as a `choice`, a `type`, or implicitly), so the `choice OffsetError` wrapper is a guess. `characters 3 until count of tz of tz` shows the `of` chain problem: the range end and the source both use `of`.
